reading.body:
Google owns this facility in Prince William County as part of a Northern Virginia campus spanning Loudoun and Prince William counties. Google announced a $1 billion expansion of this multi-county campus in April 2024, adding to existing Loudoun County data centers. The company does not publish power capacity, square footage, or individual building addresses for any of its facilities, treating this as its disclosure policy rather than withholding unresearched data.

Because Google publishes only aggregate state-level figures, the capacity of this building cannot be determined from the operator's own disclosures. Virginia's 326 mapped data center facilities include only 23 with published megawatt figures totaling 1,375 megawatts, and this site ranks 24th in the state despite being owned by one of the world's largest cloud operators. The campus is material to Virginia's AI infrastructure but its individual capacity remains opaque.

This facility's importance to AI scaling depends on facts Google has chosen not to publish: total power supply to the Northern Virginia campus, the share allocated to this Prince William County location, and the timing of the announced 2024 expansion. Without these figures, the campus cannot be ranked among competing sites or assessed for constraint on regional AI compute growth.
